🎨 DESIGN PATTERNS & SOLID PRINCIPLES - Visual Guide with Python Examples

This module provides visual representations and practical examples of:

```python
class ReportGenerator:
    """Only responsible for report generation"""

        print(f"📊 Generating report for {user.name}")

# Demo
print("\n🔴 Bad Example (Multiple Responsibilities):")
bad_user = UserManagerBad("John Doe", "john@example.com")
bad_user.save_to_database()
bad_user.send_welcome_email()

print("\n🟢 Good Example (Single Responsibility):")

repo = UserRepository()
email_service = EmailService()

if user.validate():

    email_service.send_welcome_email(user)

# 2. OPEN/CLOSED PRINCIPLE (OCP)

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("2️⃣  OPEN/CLOSED PRINCIPLE (OCP)")
print("=" * 80)
print("""
Principle: Open for EXTENSION, Closed for MODIFICATION
You should be able to extend behavior without modifying existing code.

Visual:
    ❌ BAD (Modify existing code)              ✅ GOOD (Extend through inheritance)
    
    def calculate_area(shape):                 ┌──────────────┐
        if shape.type == "circle":             │    Shape     │ (Abstract)
            return π * r²                      │──────────────│
        elif shape.type == "square":           │+ area()      │
            return side²                       └──────┬───────┘
        elif shape.type == "triangle":               │
            return 0.5 * base * height     ┌─────────┼─────────┐
        # Need to modify for new shapes! │         │         │
                                        ┌──▼───┐ ┌──▼──┐ ┌───▼────┐
                                        │Circle│ │Square│ │Triangle│
                                        │──────│ │─────│ │────────│
                                        │area()│ │area()│ │area()  │
                                        └──────┘ └─────┘ └────────┘
""")
```

sections.title: class AreaCalculatorBad, class Shape, class Circle …
class AreaCalculator
sections.body:
Works with any Shape without modification

```python
class AreaCalculator:
    """Works with any Shape without modification"""
    def calculate_total_area(self, shapes):
        return sum(shape.area() for shape in shapes)

# Demo
print("\n🟢 Good Example (Open for Extension):")
shapes = [
    Circle(5),
    Rectangle(4, 6),
    Triangle(3, 8),
    Pentagon(4)
]

calculator = AreaCalculator()
total = calculator.calculate_total_area(shapes)
print(f"📐 Total area of all shapes: {total:.2f}")

for i, shape in enumerate(shapes, 1):
    print(f"   Shape {i} ({shape.__class__.__name__}): {shape.area():.2f}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. LISKOV SUBSTITUTION PRINCIPLE (LSP)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("3️⃣  LISKOV SUBSTITUTION PRINCIPLE (LSP)")
print("=" * 80)
print("""
Principle: Objects of a superclass should be replaceable with objects of subclass
without breaking the application.

Visual:
    ❌ BAD (Breaks expectations)               ✅ GOOD (Substitutable)
    
    class Bird:                                class Bird:
        def fly(): pass                            def move(): pass
                                              
    class Penguin(Bird):                      class FlyingBird(Bird):
        def fly():                                 def fly(): pass
            raise Exception("Can't fly!")     
                                               class Penguin(Bird):
    # Breaks LSP! Penguin can't                   def swim(): pass
    # substitute Bird                         
                                               class Eagle(FlyingBird):
    ┌────────┐                                    def fly(): pass
    │  Bird  │                                
    └───┬────┘                                 ┌──────┐
        │                                      │ Bird │
    ┌───▼────┐                                 └───┬──┘
    │Penguin │ 💥 Can't fly!                       │
    └────────┘                          ┌──────────┼──────────┐
                                        │                     │
                                   ┌────▼──────┐      ┌──────▼───┐
                                   │FlyingBird │      │ Penguin  │
                                   └─────┬─────┘      │(swims)   │
                                         │            └──────────┘
                                    ┌────▼────┐
                                    │  Eagle  │
                                    │(flies)  │
                                    └─────────┘
""")
```

```python
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("4️⃣  INTERFACE SEGREGATION PRINCIPLE (ISP)")
print("=" * 80)
print("""
Principle: No client should be forced to depend on methods it doesn't use.
Split large interfaces into smaller, specific ones.

Visual:
    ❌ BAD (Fat Interface)                     ✅ GOOD (Segregated Interfaces)
    
    ┌────────────────────────┐                 ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐
    │   WorkerInterface      │                 │ Workable │  │ Eatable  │
    │────────────────────────│                 │──────────│  │──────────│
    │ + work()               │                 │+ work()  │  │+ eat()   │
    │ + eat()                │                 └────┬─────┘  └─────┬────┘
    │ + sleep()              │                      │              │
    └───────────┬────────────┘                      │              │
                │                              ┌────▼────┐    ┌────▼────┐
        ┌───────┼───────┐                     │  Human  │    │  Robot  │
        │               │                     │─────────│    │─────────│
    ┌───▼────┐     ┌────▼────┐               │+ work() │    │+ work() │
    │ Human  │     │ Robot   │               │+ eat()  │    └─────────┘
    │────────│     │─────────│               └─────────┘
    │+ work()│     │+ work() │
    │+ eat() │     │+ eat()  │ ❌ Robot doesn't eat!
    │+ sleep()│    │+ sleep()│ ❌ Robot doesn't sleep!
    └────────┘     └─────────┘
""")

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
```

class SuperRobot
sections.body:
Robot that needs maintenance (sleep)

```python
class SuperRobot(Workable, Sleepable):
    """Robot that needs maintenance (sleep)"""
    def work(self):
        return "🤖 Super robot working..."
    
    def sleep(self):
        return "🔌 Robot in maintenance mode..."

# Demo
print("\n🟢 Good Example (Segregated Interfaces):")
print("\nHuman Worker:")
human = HumanWorker()
print(f"   {human.work()}")
print(f"   {human.eat()}")
print(f"   {human.sleep()}")

print("\nBasic Robot:")
robot = RobotWorker()
print(f"   {robot.work()}")
print("   ✅ Robot doesn't need eat() or sleep() methods!")

print("\nSuper Robot:")
super_robot = SuperRobot()
print(f"   {super_robot.work()}")
print(f"   {super_robot.sleep()}")
print("   ✅ Super robot doesn't need eat() method!")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. DEPENDENCY INVERSION PRINCIPLE (DIP)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("5️⃣  DEPENDENCY INVERSION PRINCIPLE (DIP)")
print("=" * 80)
print("""
Principle: 
1. High-level modules should NOT depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions.
2. Abstractions should NOT depend on details. Details should depend on abstractions.

Visual:
    ❌ BAD (Tight Coupling)                    ✅ GOOD (Depend on Abstraction)
    
    ┌──────────────┐                           ┌──────────────┐
    │ Application  │                           │ Application  │
    │──────────────│                           │──────────────│
    │  uses        │                           │  uses        │
    └──────┬───────┘                           └──────┬───────┘
           │ (depends directly)                       │
           │                                          │ (depends on)
    ┌──────▼───────┐                           ┌──────▼───────┐
    │  MySQLDB     │                           │  Database    │ (Interface)
    │──────────────│                           │  <<abstract>>│
    │+ query()     │                           │──────────────│
    └──────────────┘                           │+ query()     │
                                               └──────┬───────┘
    # Hard to switch database! ❌                     │
                                          ┌────────────┼──────────┐
                                          │                       │
                                    ┌─────▼─────┐         ┌──────▼─────┐
                                    │  MySQL    │         │ PostgreSQL │
                                    │───────────│         │────────────│
                                    │+ query()  │         │+ query()   │
                                    └───────────┘         └────────────┘
                                    
                                    Easy to switch! ✅
""")

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
```

class UserRepository
sections.body:
High-level module depends on abstraction

```python
class UserRepository:
    """High-level module depends on abstraction"""
    def __init__(self, database: Database):
        self.db = database  # Depends on abstraction! ✅
        print(self.db.connect())
    
    def get_user(self, user_id):
        result = self.db.query(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id={user_id}")
        return result

# Demo
print("\n🟢 Good Example (Dependency Inversion):")
print("\nUsing MySQL:")
mysql_repo = UserRepository(MySQLDatabase())
print(f"   {mysql_repo.get_user(1)}")

print("\nUsing PostgreSQL:")
postgres_repo = UserRepository(PostgreSQLDatabase())
print(f"   {postgres_repo.get_user(1)}")

print("\nUsing MongoDB:")
mongo_repo = UserRepository(MongoDatabase())
print(f"   {mongo_repo.get_user(1)}")

print("\n✅ Easy to switch databases without changing UserRepository!")

print("1️⃣  SINGLETON PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("""
Purpose: Ensure a class has only ONE instance and provide global access to it.

Visual:
    ┌─────────────────────────┐
    │      Singleton          │
    │─────────────────────────│
    │ - instance: Singleton   │ (static)
    │─────────────────────────│
    │ + getInstance()         │
    └─────────────────────────┘
              │
              │ Always returns
              │ same instance
              ▼
         [●] Instance
         
    Client 1 ──┐
    Client 2 ──┼──► [●] Same Instance
    Client 3 ──┘

Use Cases:
- Database connections
- Configuration managers
- Logger instances
- Cache managers
- Thread pools
""")
```

sections.title: class SingletonMeta, class DatabaseConnection
class Logger
sections.body:
Logger - only one instance needed

```python
class Logger(metaclass=SingletonMeta):
    """Logger - only one instance needed"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.logs = []
        print("📝 Creating new logger...")
    
    def log(self, message):
        self.logs.append(message)
        print(f"   LOG: {message}")
    
    def get_logs(self):
        return self.logs

# Demo
print("\n🔍 Testing Singleton Pattern:")
print("\nAttempting to create multiple database connections:")
db1 = DatabaseConnection()
db2 = DatabaseConnection()
db3 = DatabaseConnection()

print(f"\n✅ db1 is db2: {db1 is db2}")
print(f"✅ db2 is db3: {db2 is db3}")
print(f"✅ All are same instance: {id(db1) == id(db2) == id(db3)}")

print("\nTesting with Logger:")
logger1 = Logger()
logger1.log("First message")

logger2 = Logger()
logger2.log("Second message")

print(f"\n✅ logger1 is logger2: {logger1 is logger2}")
print(f"✅ Logs in logger1: {len(logger1.get_logs())}")
print(f"✅ Logs in logger2: {len(logger2.get_logs())}")

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. FACTORY PATTERN
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("2️⃣  FACTORY PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("""
Purpose: Create objects without specifying exact class to create.

Visual:
              ┌──────────────┐
              │   Factory    │
              │──────────────│
              │+ create()    │
              └──────┬───────┘
                     │ creates
         ┌───────────┼───────────┐
         │           │           │
    ┌────▼────┐ ┌────▼────┐ ┌────▼────┐
    │Product A│ │Product B│ │Product C│
    └─────────┘ └─────────┘ └─────────┘

Use Cases:
- Creating different types of documents (PDF, Word, Excel)
- Creating different payment methods (Credit Card, PayPal, Bitcoin)
- Creating different notification channels (Email, SMS, Push)
""")

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
```
